• It is celebrated during the month of April for symbolizing the unity of saivitism and Vaishnavism.
 
• It celebrates for fifteen days.
 
• According to the Tamil calendar, Chithirai is the first month of the year.
 
• On this day Lord Vishnu comes to attend the marriage ceremony of her sister and Lord Sundreshwar, which is celebrated as Chithirai.
 
• During the Chithirai festival, many events take place.
 
• The first event that takes place in the whole celebration of the Chithirai festival is the "Kodi Yetram".
 
• In Kodi Yetram the chief priest of Meenakshi temple declares the opening of the festival by hoisting the flag on the flag post of the temple.

questions.question: Kalbelia dance is generally performed in which of the following states of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Kalbelia Dance: A Traditional Dance from Rajasthan**

__
 
• Kalbelia dance is a special dance from Rajasthan, India.
 
• It's also called the 'Snake Charmer Dance.'
 
• People from the Kalbelia tribe (The Snake Experts) perform this dance.
 
 
• They used to catch snakes and sell their venom.
 
• This unique job has influenced their dance and culture.
 
 
 
• It got famous worldwide and is recognized by UNESCO since 2010.
 
• The main instrument is called 'Poongi' or 'Been,' which is like a musical pipe.
 
• Other instruments like drums, tambourines, and more are used.
 
• Women are usually the dancers. They move like snakes while dancing. Their clothes are special: a top, a headscarf, and a long skirt.
 
• The clothes are mostly black with red decorations and shiny thread patterns. They wear traditional jewelry and sometimes even mirrors on their clothes.
 
• There's no school or written lessons for this dance. The knowledge is shared by talking and showing to the next generation.

questions.question: The rule of the English East India company was ended in British India under the Government of India Act, ______.
questions.solution:
the correct answer is __**1858**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The rule of the English East India Company ended in British India under the Government of India Act of 1858. Under this Act, the governance of India was transferred from the company to the British Crown, marking the start of the period of direct rule, also known as the British Raj.

**key features of the Government of India Act of 1858**:

 
• **End of East India Company Rule**: The Act, coming into force on **2 August 1858**, ended the rule of the East India Company after nearly 250 years of control over Indian territories.
 
• **Secretary of State for India**: The Act introduced a new official post, the Secretary of State for India, who was a member of the British cabinet. He was given complete control over Indian administration and was aided by a **15-member Council of India**.
 
• **Change in Governance Structure**: The Governor-General of India, who was now also identified as the Viceroy of India, was the representative of the Crown in India and was responsible for the executive administration of the Indian provinces. This change **ended the old "double government" system **where the Board of Control and the Court of Directors administrating different roles.
 
• **Retention of Company Troops**: Approximately **260,000 soldiers** of the existing East India Company became soldiers of the Crown.
 
• **End of Doctrine of Lapse**: The 1858 Act **ended **the much-disputed **Doctrine of Lapse, introduced by Lord Dalhousie in 1848, **under which the British annexed any princely state whose ruler was either "manifestly incompetent" or died without a male heir.
 
• **Legal Reform**: With this transition, a comprehensive legal system was enforced, including the** introduction of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) in 1860**.
 
• **Civil Services**: The Act **opened doors to the institutionalization of the Indian Civil Services**. Although Indians could sit for the civil services examinations after this Act,** until 1922**. Indians could appear in the Indian Civil Service Examinations which were held in England.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Wars**:

 
• **Anglo-Afghan Wars**: These wars were fought between British India and Afghanistan. By 1858, the first of these wars (1839-1842) had already concluded with a humiliating retreat for the British. Two more Anglo-Afghan Wars would follow in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
 
• **Anglo-Sikh Wars**: There were two Anglo-Sikh Wars. The First Anglo-Sikh War (1845-46) and the Second Anglo-Sikh War (1848-49). As a result of these wars, the Sikh Empire was annexed by the British East India Company.
 
• **Burma Wars**: The Second Anglo-Burmese War (1852) led to the British East India Company's annexation of the lower Burma. The third war (1885) would result in the total annexation of Burma by the British.

**Social Changes**:

 
• **Education Policies**: The British tried to reform the education system, grounding it in Western philosophy and ideals. The **University of Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras were established in 1857.**
 
• **Social Reforms**: Under the British rule, several old Indian social practices were challenged. For instance, **the practice of Sati (the self-immolation of a widow on her husband's funeral pyre) was outlawed by Governor-General William Bentinck in 1829.**
 
• **Religious Changes**: Christian missionaries were more** freely allowed to propagate Christianity**, leading to a growth of this minority religion in different parts of India.
 
• **Infrastructure**: Infrastructure, including roads and railways, telegraph and postal services were expanded, largely aimed at securing and supporting British military and administrative control.
 
• **Introduction of the Railways**: The first passenger railway in India was opened in 1853, prior to the Government of India Act,** between Bombay and Thane**.

questions.question: The famous scientist, Albert Einstein, was inspired by whose idea of non - violence?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Albert Einstein was known to greatly admire the philosophy and principles advocated by Mahatma Gandhi, particularly the concept of non-violence or "ahimsa".
 
• He had corresponded with Gandhi and expressed his admiration.
 
• There is a famous quote attributed to Einstein about Gandhi: "Generations to come, it may well be, will scarce believe that such a man as this one ever in flesh and blood walked upon this Earth".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vardhaman Mahavira**

 
 
• Born in 599 BCE in Kundalagrama, Bihar, in a royal family of the Kshatriya clan.
 
• Mahavira means "Great Hero" – a title he earned through his teachings. He's often referred to as 'Jain' since his followers are called 'Jains'.
 
• Became the 24th Tirthankara (religious teacher) of Jainism at around age 42 after 12 years of rigorous ascetic practices.
 
• He propagated the principle of Ahimsa (non-violence), truth, asceticism, and righteousness.
 
• His teachings included the central tenet of Jainism: the Three Jewels, or right faith, right knowledge, and right conduct.
 
• Mahavira is traditionally believed to have been born in 599 BCE and to have achieved Nirvana (release from the cycle of birth and death) in 527 BCE.
 
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**
 
 
• Born on 2nd October 1869, in Porbandar, Gujarat is celebrated as the International Day of Non-Violence.
 
• Led famous movements against the British rule, such as Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22), Civil Disobedience Movement (1930), and Quit India Movement (1942), which resulted in India's independence in 1947.
 
• Assassinated on 30th January 1948, by Nathuram Godse.
 
• His philosophy of peaceful resistance, known as Satyagraha, has inspired civil rights movements worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Gautam Buddha**
 
 
• Siddhartha Gautama, known as the Buddha, was the founder of Buddhism.
 
• He was born as a prince in Lumbini (present-day Nepal) but renounced his royal life when confronted with the realities of human suffering.
 
• His teachings, known as Dhamma in Buddhism, includes the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path, which articulate the reality of suffering and the path to the cessation of suffering.
 
• Established the Sangha, an order of monks, for the spread of his teachings.
 
• Buddha is believed to have attained Nirvana (Enlightenment) under the Bodhi tree at Bodhgaya, Bihar, India.
 
 
 
• **B. R. Ambedkar**
 
 
• Full name Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar, often known as Babasaheb, he was an Indian jurist, economist, and social reformer.
 
• He played a pivotal role in drafting the Indian constitution and is widely known as the "Father of the Indian Constitution."
 
• As a leading activist and social reformer, Ambedkar campaigned against social discrimination towards the untouchables (Dalits).
 
• He led the Mahad Satyagraha on 20th March 1927 to allow untouchables to use water from a public tank in Mahad, Maharashtra.
 
• As the first Minister of Law and Justice of India, he played a key role in drafting the Indian Constitution.
 
• He was also the one to lead Dalit Buddhist Movement in 1956 in India for the rights and upliftment of Dalits. His death anniversary on 6th December is observed as "Mahaparinirvan Diwas" across India.

questions.question: Which of the following is INCORRECTLY matched?

options.text: Mountain climate - Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Jharkhand
Tropical monsoon climate - The Western Ghats, the Malabar Coast and southern Assam
Tropical semi-arid (steppe) climate - Karnataka, central Maharashtra, some parts of Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh
Hot deserts, arid climate - Rajasthan and some parts of Gujarat

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Montane climate - Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Jharkhand**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Mountain ****Climate**: This is not exactly a category on Köppen’s climate classification but is typically characterized by cooler temperatures due to higher altitudes, and it is associated with mountainous regions.

 
 
• Examples can be found in the Himalayan range, parts of the Andes, and the Rocky Mountains.
 
 
 
• Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Jharkhand are not predominantly mountainous regions.
 
• More accurately, the montane climate is seen in states like Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, and parts of states like Jammu & Kashmir or Ladakh, where the Himalayan range is present.

Therefore, this matching of **"Montane Climate - Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Jharkhand" is incorrectly matched**.<span style=&quo

questions.question: Who among the following has been appointed as the new Chairperson of the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT), for a period of four years or until he attains the age of 70 years, whichever is the earliest in November 2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Justice Ashok Bhushan**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Govt. appoints Justice Ashok Bhushan as NCLAT chairperson, Justice R. Sudhakar as NCLT president.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) is a crucial quasi-judicial body in India. Here are some essential points about NCLAT which would be useful from an exam perspective:
 
• **Establishment**: NCLAT was constituted under Section 410 of the Companies Act, 2013 for hearing appeals against the orders of National Company Law Tribunal(s) (NCLT).
 
• **Date of Creation**: NCLAT was established on 1st June 2016.
 
• **Function**: NCLAT hears appeals against the orders of NCLT under Section 61 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC). It also hears appeals against the decisions of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India.
 
• **Jurisdiction**: In addition to company law disputes, NCLAT also hears appeals from orders issued by the Competition Commission of India (CCI).
 
• **Chairperson**: The Chairperson of NCLAT is appointed by the President of India.
 
• **Members**: NCLAT consists of a chairperson, judicial members, and technical members.
 
• **Term of Office**: As per the rules, the term of office for the Chairperson and members is five years or till they attain 70 years of age, whichever is earlier [1].
 
• **Appeals**: Orders of NCLAT can be appealed in the Supreme Court of India.
 
• **Significance**: NCLAT plays a critical role in India's legal landscape by ensuring that companies follow laws and regulations, and it provides a vital mechanism for resolving disputes under the Companies Act, 2013 and the IBC, 2016 efficiently and quickly.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT included in domestic income?

options.text: Income earned by the residents of the country
Income earned by the non-residents outside the country
Income earned by all the employees of the country
Profit of all the industries of the country

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Income earned by the non-residents outside the country**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Domestic income, also known as Gross Domestic Product, is the total income earned by all sectors (households, firms, and the government) within the geographical boundaries of a country, irrespective of whether they are residents or non-residents.
 
• However, income earned by non-residents outside the country is NOT included in the domestic income. Such income is part of the national income, not domestic income.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**: This is the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders over a specific period, typically a year.
 
• **Gross National Product (GNP)**: It is the total market value of all final goods and services produced by residents of a country in a given period of time.
 
 
• **GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA)**
 
• Here, **Net Factor Income from Abroad = Income earned by domestic factors of production from rest of the world - Income earned by factors of production of rest of the world from the domestic economy**
 
 
 
• **Net National Product (NNP) at Factor Cost or National Income (NI)**: This is the GNP minus depreciation.
 
 
• NNP or NI = GNP - Depreciation
 
 
 
• **Net Domestic Product (NDP)**: This is the GDP minus depreciation.
 
 
• NDP = GDP - Depreciation
 
 
 
• **Per Capita Income**: It is a measure of the amount of money earned per person in a certain area.
 
 
• Per Capita Income = National Income / Total Population
 
 
 
• **Factor Income**: It's the income that factors of production (land, labour, capital, and entrepreneurship) receive in return for their contribution to the production process.
 
• **Transfer Payments:** These are payments made without the provision of goods or services in return. Examples are social security benefits, pensions, unemployment benefits, etc. Transfer payments are not included in the computation of national income as they do not involve productive activity.

questions.question: As per National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) 2019 - 21, what percentage of women have a bank or savings account that they themselves use?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**78.6%**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya released the National Report of the fifth round of National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5).
 
• The report comprises of detailed information on key domains of population, health and family welfare and associated domains like characteristics of the population; fertility; family planning; infant and child mortality; maternal and child health; nutrition and anaemia; morbidity and healthcare; women’s empowerment etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

The **National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) 2019-2021** has many **key findings**, including: 

 
• The sex ratio was **1,020 women for every 1,000 men**. 
 
• The under-five** mortality rate** dropped from 50 deaths per 1,000 live births in 2015-16 to 42 deaths per 1,000 in 2019-21.
 
• The **infant mortality rate **also declined from 41 deaths per 1,000 live births to 35 deaths per 1,000 live births. 
 
• The percentage of 20–24 year old girls who **married** before age 18 decreased from 26.8% to 23.3%. 
 
• The **adolescent fertility rate** (women aged 15–19) decreased from 51% to 43%.

questions.question: Tansen, who was included in the Navaratnas of Akbar, was an expert in playing which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rabab**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Tansen, one of the Navaratnas of Akbar's court, was a notable figure in Hindustani classical music.
 
• He was an exceptional vocalist and is also known for his expertise in playing the Rudra Veena or "Rabab" an ancient Indian string instrument.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Akbar's Navaratnas, or Nine Jewels, were a group of nine talented individuals at the court of the Mughal Emperor Akbar. Each of them was well known for their respective skills and contributions. They were:

 
• **Abul Fazl (also known as Allami)**: The full name of** Abul Fazl is Abu'l-Fazl ibn Mubarak**. He was one of the most important historians during the reign of Akbar. His most known writings are the **Akbarnama and the Ain-i-Akbari**. Akbarnama is a historical account of Akbar's reign, and Ain-i-Akbari is a detailed document recording the administration of the empire.
 
• **Faizi (or Shaikh Faiz)**: His real name was Shaikh Faizi Sirhindi. He was a brilliant poet and scholar. He is known for his poetry collection called **"Taskeen-e-ruh-o-dil"** and also his interpretation of ancient texts.
 
• **Raja Birbal (originally named Mahesh Das)**: He was a poet and musician, admired for his quick wit, intelligence and his keen sense of humor. Among his notable contributions are the Birbal stories, popular folklore that's been passed down generations.
 
• **Raja Todar Mal (Todar Mall)**: He was a finance minister **(Diwan-i-Ashraff)** who undertook innovative measures like standardizing land measurements to improve the revenue system. He doesn't have any known books or musical contributions.
 
• **Tansen (originally named Ramtanu Pandey)**: He was associated with the Dhrupad style and a pioneer of Indian classical music. He composed many ragas which are still in use today.
 
• **Raja Man Singh (Man Singh I)**: He led many successful military campaigns for Emperor Akbar. He was influential in the administration and politics.
 
• **Abdul Rahim Khan-I-Khana (Rahim)**: He is known for his 'dohas' or couplings in Hindi. He is also known for translating Babar's memoirs, Baburnama from Chagatai language to Persian.
 
• **Fakir Aziao-Din**: He was one of the chief advisors to Akbar and was highly respected for his wisdom and spirituality. 
 
• **Mullah Do Piaza**: His contributions are mainly in the form of folklore, with stories about his wisdom and wit being highlighted in Mughal anecdotes.

• Globally, 17 countries, including China, Hungary, Montenegro, Uzbekistan, Russia and Saudi Arabia, shared the top spot.

questions.question: Mitochondria is NOT found in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**bacteria**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mitochondria are not found in bacteria**.
 
• Bacteria are prokaryotic cells and do not contain organelles, such as mitochondria, that are found in eukaryotic cells.
 
• It's interesting to note that it's widely accepted that mitochondria originated from a type of prokaryote due to a symbiotic event in the distant past, a theory known as endosymbiosis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****​​Mitochondria:**

 
• **Cell Organelle**: Mitochondria are cell organelles in eukaryotic cells. They are not present in prokaryotic cells like bacteria.
 
• Structure: Each mitochondrion is a double-membrane-bound structure with the outer membrane being smooth and the inner one thrown into folds or cristae.
 
• **Powerhouse of the Cell**: Mitochondria are often referred to as the 'powerhouse of the cell'. They are the sites of cellular respiration and produce energy in the form of ATP (adenosine triphosphate).
 
• **Semi-Autonomous**: Mitochondria are semi-autonomous organelles. They have their own DNA and ribosomes, meaning they can manufacture their own proteins and replicate independently of the cell in which they reside. This suggests a symbiotic origin to the mitochondria, supporting the endosymbiotic theory.
 
• **Number of Mitochondria**: The number of mitochondria in a cell can vary greatly depending on the cell type. For example, cells with high energy needs like muscle cells have more mitochondria, while other cells may have very few.
 
• **Size and Shape**: Mitochondria are typically rod-shaped or oval in nature. Their size ranges from 0.5 to 1.0 micrometre in diameter.
 
• **Role in Metabolism**: Mitochondria are not only the energy factories of the cell, but also participate in other metabolic tasks such as the synthesis of certain components of blood and hormones, the metabolism of cholesterol, and the regulation of calcium concentration in the cell.
 
• **Cytochromes**: Mitochondria contain a number of enzymes, including the cytochromes, which participate in electron transport during aerobic respiration.
 
• **Matrix Space**: The space within the inner membrane of a mitochondrion is known as the matrix. It contains a number of enzymes, the mitochondrial DNA, ribosomes, and granules that store calcium phosphate.
 
• **Oxysomes or F1 Particles**: The inner membrane of mitochondria bears some spherical bodies called oxysomes or F1 particles. These particles are involved directly in ATP synthesis.
 
• **Krebs Cycle**: The process by which energy is produced in the mitochondria, the Krebs (or citric acid) cycle, is a series of biochemical reactions that generate energy through the oxidation of acetate—derived from carbohydrates, fats, and proteins—into carbon dioxide.
 
• **Mitochondrial Disorders**: Certain genetic disorders have been linked to mutations in mitochondrial DNA. These include some forms of heart disease, diabetes, and Leigh's syndrome, a progressive neurometabolic disorder.
 
• **Role in Aging**: Some theories suggest a role for mitochondria in the aging process. The free-radical theory of aging suggests that accumulated damage from oxidative stress (the imbalance between the production of free radicals and the ability of cells to counteract their harmful effects), largely caused by mitochondria, results in the physiological changes we associate with aging.
 
• **Mitophagy**: The process in which defective mitochondria are destroyed by cellular machinery is termed 'mitophagy'. This is a vital process as it assists in maintaining the proper functioning of cells by removing damaged mitochondria that could potentially harm the cell.

questions.question:
Which of the following pairs is/are correctly matched regarding the terminology used in the Parliament?

A. Appropriation Bill - A Money Bill passed for providing for the withdrawal or appropriation from and out of the Consolidated Fund of India

B. Demand for Grants - Earmarking of budgetary allocation for meeting only planned expenditure of a Ministry/Department

C. Short Duration Discussion - For raising a discussion on a matter of urgent public importance for which a notice has to be given by a Member and supported by 50 Members
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A only**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A. Appropriation Bill - The Appropriation Bill is indeed a Money Bill passed for providing for the withdrawal or appropriation from and out of the Consolidated Fund of India. Therefore, this option is correctly matched.
 
• B. Demand for Grants and C. Short Duration Discussion - are incorrectly paired in the context provided.
 
 
• The "Demands for Grants" are the estimates of expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India, presented to the Lok Sabha for its approval. The demands are presented ministry-wise.
 
• A "Short Duration Discussion" in the Indian parliament refers to a discussion on a matter of urgent public importance, which can be raised with prior notice, but it does not need to be supported by 50 members, so again the pairing is incorrect.
 
 
 
• So, based on the given pairs, the correct answer is "A only".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Money Bill**: Any bill that pertains to taxation and government finances is classified as a Money Bill under Article 110. The Speaker of the Lok Sabha holds the authority to decide whether a financial bill is a Money Bill or not. In the case of Money Bills, the Rajya Sabha (Upper House) has limited powers—all amendments recommended by Rajya Sabha are not binding on Lok Sabha.
 
• **Ordinance**: Under Article 123, the President of India is empowered to issue ordinances when Parliament is not in session, and immediate legislative action is needed. However, such an ordinance must be approved by the Parliament within six weeks of its next session.
 
• **Question Hour**: This is the first hour of a parliamentary sitting/session where Members of Parliament ask questions to ministers and hold them accountable for the functioning of their ministries.
 
• **Zero Hour**: Unlike the Question Hour, the Zero Hour is not mentioned in any rules of procedure. Thus, it is an informal but powerful tool available to the members of the Parliament to raise matters of great importance without any prior notice.
 
• **Quorum (Article 100)**: This refers to the minimum number of Members of Parliament that must be present to make the proceedings of that House valid. In India, the quorum to conduct a meeting of either House of Parliament is one-tenth of the total number of seats in that House.
 
• **Powers, Privileges, etc. of Parliament Members (Article 105)**: According to this article, the Parliament and its members and committees have powers and privileges that are necessary for the exercise of their responsibilities. No Member of Parliament can be held liable in any court for anything that is said, or any vote given, in Parliament or its committee meetings.
 
• **Motion of No Confidence**: This is a statement or vote that states or proposes that a government must be called into account. A motion of no confidence mandates the government to prove its majority in the house.
 
• **Private Member's Bill**: Any bill introduced by a Member of Parliament who is not a minister is called a private member's bill. These bills are treated the same as other public bills, but in practicality, they have little chance of being passed due to lower precedence on the legislative agenda.
 
• **Cut Motions**: These are objections raised in Lok Sabha to the demand made for grants, essentially objections to the amount of financial expenditure.

questions.question: Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Puraskar) for the year 2020 was awarded to Meenakshi Chitharanjan for her contribution to which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Puraskar) for the year 2020 was awarded to Meenakshi Chitharanjan for her contribution to Bharatanatyam.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, also known as the Akademi Puraskar, is the highest national recognition given to practicing artists in India. The award is bestowed by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy of Music, Dance & Drama, which is an autonomous body of the Ministry of Culture, Government of India.

Here are some key points about the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award:

 
• Establishment: The award was established in 1952 and is conferred by the President of India.
 
• Fields of Recognition: It recognizes outstanding contributions in the field of music, dance, and drama/theatre. The music category includes Carnatic music, Hindustani music, and other traditional music forms. Dance recognitions include major Indian classical dance forms and folk dances. Drama recognition spans from playwriting to acting, directing, and even puppetry.
 
• Components of the Award: The award comprises a purse of Rs. 1,00,000, a citation, an angavastram (a ceremonial shawl), and a tamrapatra (a brass plaque).
 
• Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar: This is a special award by the Sangeet Natak Akademi to recognize and encourage outstanding young talents in the field of performing arts.
 
• Fellowship of the academy: The Fellowship of the Sangeet Natak Akademi, restricted to a very limited number at a given time, is the highest honour in the performing arts conferred by the Government of India.
 
• Awarding Process: The General Council of the Akademi makes the final decision regarding the awardees, based on the recommendations of its advisory committees.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement about Phylum Arthropoda.

options.text: Class Insecta is the largest class of Phylum Arthropoda.
Lignin is the main component of the exoskeletons of arthropods.
Over 85% of all the known animal species are arthropods.
Phylum Arthropoda comprises a wide diversity of animals with hard exoskeletons and jointed appendages.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lignin is the main component of the exoskeletons of arthropods.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bacteria are a separate domain of life and are not related to the phylum Arthropoda.
 
• Arthropoda is the phylum that includes insects, spiders, crustaceans, and other similar creatures, all of which are multicellular and have exoskeletons, segmented bodies, and paired, jointed appendages. In contrast, bacteria are unicellular microorganisms in the domain Bacteria.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Phylum Arthropoda**:

 
• Arthropods are the most diverse group of animals, representing over 80% of known living animal species.
 
• Arthropods are characterized by their jointed legs (from which their name derives: 'arthro' means jointed, 'pod' means legs) and a hard exoskeleton made primarily of chitin.
 
• The exoskeleton serves as both a protective structure and a surface for muscle attachment, but it also needs to be periodically shed and regrown through a process called molting as the animal grows.
 
• The specifics of the body plan vary between arthropods, but generally, they possess a segmented body divided into regions such as the head, thorax, and abdomen. Some species may have a fused head and thorax known as a cephalothorax.
 
• Arthropods have specialized, paired appendages. These are often adapted for roles including sensory reception, feeding, and locomotion.
 
• Arthropoda has a broad range of ecological roles, from insects pollinating flowers to spiders acting as predators.
 
• Arthropoda is further divided into several subgroups or classes, like Insecta (insects), Arachnida (spiders and scorpions), Myriapoda (centipedes and millipedes), and Crustacea (crabs, lobsters, shrimp).
 
• In contrast, bacteria refer to microscopic, single-celled organisms belonging to the domain Bacteria. They are completely separate from arthropods and represent one of the most basic forms of life. They have a cell wall but lack organized nuclei and other cell organelles.

questions.question: ______ countries participated in the Tokyo Paralympic 2020.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**162**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Tokyo 2020 Paralympic Games, which were actually held in 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic, saw participation from **162 National Paralympic Committees, including a refugee team.**
 
• **Avani Lekhara**: This Indian shooter made history by becoming the first Indian woman to win a gold medal at the Paralympics. She achieved this in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event, equaling the world record score of 249.6.
 
• **Sumit Antil**: In men's javelin throw F64, Antil not only won the gold medal but also set a new world record with his throw of 68.55 meters.
 
• **Manish Narwal**: In the mixed 50m pistol SH1 event, Narwal secured a gold medal with a Paralympic record of 218.2 points.
 
• **Krishna Nagar**: Competing in the Men's singles SH6 category in badminton, Nagar won gold for India.
 
• **Pramod Bhagat**: Another star in badminton, Bhagat won gold in men's singles SL3 event.
 
• **Singhraj Adana**: Winning a bronze in the P1 men's 10m air pistol SH1, Adana followed up with a silver in the P4 mixed 50m pistol SH1 event.
 
• **Mariyappan Thangavelu and Sharad Kumar**: In the men's high jump T42 category, Thangavelu and Kumar won silver and bronze for India respectively.
 
• **Devendra Jhajharia**: The veteran javelin thrower won silver in the men's javelin throw F46, which was his third Paralympic medal.
 
• **Sundar Singh Gurjar**: Along with Jhajharia in the men's javelin throw F46 category, Gurjar picked up a bronze medal.

questions.question: Who sent the Greek ambassador Megasthenes to the court of Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seleucus**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Megasthenes was sent to the court of Chandragupta Maurya by Seleucus I Nicator.
 
• Seleucus I Nicator was one of the generals of Alexander the Great who, after Alexander's death, took control of the eastern part of his empire, which included territories in Asia Minor, Persia, and parts of India.
 
• Seleucus I Nicator and Chandragupta Maurya signed a treaty, following which Megasthenes was sent as an ambassador from the Seleucid Dynasty to the Mauryan Empire.
 
• Megasthenes is known for his important work "Indica," a record of his observations about India's geography, culture, and society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Megasthenes wrote an account of his observations about India in his book named "Indica"**..

 
• **Geographical Details**: Megasthenes provided an account of India's geography, including its mountains, rivers, flora and fauna, and climatic conditions.
 
• **Description of Society**: "Indica" included distinct details about social divisions, including the caste system and occupations of various groups.
 
• **Urban Centers**: Megasthenes described the city of Pataliputra (modern Patna), capital of the Maurya empire, in detail. This gave us information about city life, architecture, and administration.
 
• **Administration and Military**: The book portrayed the organized administrative structures and gave an account of the Mauryan army, with descriptions of elephants in warfare.
 
• **Customs and Practices**: "Indica" included information about contemporary customs, diets, festivals, and religious practices, and reported that India had no slavery.
 
• Megasthenes also provided an account of Chandragupta Maurya’s reign and wrote about the prosperity and peace within the empire.
 
• It is important to note that "Indica" had some inaccuracies or exaggerations possibly due to misunderstandings or cultural differences. For example, **Megasthenes reported on creatures such as giant ants that dug up gold dust and humans with no mouths,** which are widely considered to be based on misunderstandings or myths.

**Chandragupta Maurya (ruled c. 321–c. 297 BCE) was the founder of the Maurya Empire in India. His reign was noted for its significant expansion, political unity, administration and development of infrastructure.**

 
• Chandragupta Maurya overthrew the Nanda Dynasty in Magadh with the help of his advisor, Chanakya (Kautilya), and began his rule.
 
• He had a vast empire that included large parts of India, extending to Persia and parts of Afghanistan in the west.
 
• Chandragupta's administration was centralized. The Mauryan administration, as described in Kautilya's Arthashastra, had a highly organized bureaucratic structure with a council of ministers.
 
• He had a standing army and implemented an efficient revenue collection system.
 
• Chandragupta is said to have embraced Jainism towards the end of his life and undertook a fasting ritual until death, as per Jain tradition, at a place called Shravanabelagola in present-day Karnataka, India.
 
• Chandragupta's rule was succeeded by his son Bindusara, and then by his famous grandson, Ashoka.

questions.question: Which of the following amendment acts included Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 42nd Amendment Act**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Fundamental Duties of citizens were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976, during the period of the Emergency (1975-77). This was done upon the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee that was constituted by the government in 1976.
 
• The Committee had recommended the inclusion of a separate chapter in the Constitution on Fundamental Duties. As a result, Part IVA was inserted into the Constitution, with Article 51A defining the Fundamental Duties.
 
• These Duties were designed to promote patriotism among citizens and ensure an active involvement of the citizens in the nation's democratic processes. As originally incorporated, there were ten Fundamental Duties. Here they are for reference:
 
 
• To respect the Constitution, National Flag, and National Anthem.
 
• To respect the ideals of freedom struggle.
 
• To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• To defend the country and render national service when called upon.
 
• To promote harmony and brotherhood among all the people.
 
• To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
 
• To protect and improve the natural environment.
 
• To develop the scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
• To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
 
• To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity.
 
 
 
• Later, the 86th Amendment Act in 2002 added one more duty:
 
 
• Parent or guardian is to provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years.
 
 
 
• However, unlike the Fundamental Rights which are enforceable by the courts, the Fundamental Duties are unenforceable by the law. The Constitution does not provide any direct mechanism for their enforcement. Nevertheless, they serve as a constant reminder to citizens of the expectations that the nation has from them and the responsibilities they need to fulfill to ensure the fruition of their rights.

questions.question: Which of the following states recognise the Dahi Handi as a sports event?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dahi Handi is recognised as an adventure sport in the state of Maharashtra, India.
 
• This decision was taken by the Maharashtra government to ensure the safety regulations are adhered to during the event, as it involves forming a human pyramid which often leads to the possibility of injuries.
 
• The sport is traditionally played during the celebration of Janmashtami, the birthday of Lord Krishna, reflecting his childhood mischief of stealing curd and butter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Event Name
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Dahi Handi
 Associated with Krishna Janmashtami, this event involves forming a pyramid of people to break a pot hung high in the air, mirroring the antics of Lord Krishna in his youth. This event is particularly popular in Maharashtra.
 
 

 Jallikattu
 Conducted during Pongal celebrations in Tamil Nadu, Jallikattu is a bull-taming event. It's a part of the centuries-old Tamil cultural heritage.
 
 

 Rath Yatra Chariot Race
 This event occurs during the Ratha Yatra, a public procession with chariots of deities, primarily held in Odisha, dedicated to Lord Jagannath (Lord Krishna), his sister Subhadra, and his elder brother Balabhadra (Balarama).
 
 

 Sikh Games or Gatka
 Gatka is a traditional martial art associated with Sikhism, often performed during religious processions. It is also competitively performed in an arena in tournaments and events known as Sikh games.
 
 

 Onam Boat Races
 These races are a part of Onam celebrations in Kerala. Snake boats (Chundan Vallam) and other types of traditional boats participate in these exhilarating races. The most famous among them is the Nehru Trophy Boat Race.
 
 

 Rural Olympics in Kila Raipur
 This sports festival is held annually in Kila Raipur (near Ludhiana) in Punjab, featuring rural sports like cart-racing, tug-of-war, and feats of strength and agility. Though not directly religious, it is deeply interconnected with Punjabi and Sikh culture.
